questions.q: What determines which fields you're allowed to filter on when running plain SOQL against a custom Big Object?
options: Any field marked as 'Filterable' in the object's page layout
The object's defined index, which also acts as its primary key
Whichever fields are marked required
There is no restriction — Big Objects support the same filtering as standard objects
questions.explain: A Big Object's index defines its identity and constrains what SOQL can filter on, generally requiring filters to start from the first indexed field. This makes index design the central decision when building a custom Big Object.

questions.q: What happened to Async SOQL, and what's the current recommended approach for large-scale processing of Big Object data beyond indexed SOQL?
options: Async SOQL is still fully supported and recommended as the primary tool
Async SOQL was retired from all orgs in 2023; Batch Apex and the Bulk API are the current approaches
Async SOQL was renamed to 'Big SOQL' with no functional change
Async SOQL was replaced by unrestricted standard SOQL on Big Objects
questions.explain: Salesforce retired Async SOQL from all orgs in 2023. Batch Apex and the Bulk API are the current tools for large-volume processing against Big Object data.

questions.q: An External Object configured through Salesforce Connect's OData adapter displays data from a vendor platform inside a related list on the Policy record. What is actually happening on each read?
options: Salesforce silently replicates the vendor data into a hidden custom object overnight
The related list is reading from a nightly batch sync stored in Salesforce
Each read is a live callout to the external system — no copy of the data is stored in Salesforce
External Objects can only be viewed through a separate dedicated tab, never in a related list
questions.explain: An External Object maps to data that lives and is maintained in the outside system; every read is a live callout rather than a query against a Salesforce-stored copy.

questions.q: Which of these is the standard Big Object Salesforce itself ships, used for long-term field-history retention?
options: AuditTrail__b
FieldHistoryArchive
RecordHistoryLog__b
ComplianceEvents
questions.explain: FieldHistoryArchive is Salesforce's standard Big Object, part of the Field Audit Trail feature, used to retain field history for long-term audit and compliance purposes.

questions.q: A dataset is owned and actively maintained by a separate, vendor-hosted claims system, and adjusters need current (not replicated) visibility into it from Salesforce. Which approach fits, per this lesson's decision rule?
options: A custom Big Object, since the data volume is likely large
A standard custom object with a nightly sync job
An External Object, since the data is owned and maintained outside Salesforce and needs live access
Custom Metadata Types, since the data is configuration-like
questions.explain: Per the lesson's decision rule, data owned and maintained outside Salesforce that needs current, non-replicated access is the External Object use case — Big Objects are for data generated and owned inside Salesforce.
